problems.problem: Logging is below the 95% threshold (G5 fails). The Individual Motivation certification request and the reason question 'What is your reason, in a few words?' have no question records. The Search 3 DRAFT reading (one PCOS review protocol) has no draft record. Msg 22's added question is not logged.
problems.cause: Kit: k.certify_line does not log a question. When k.certify receives 'certify' without a reason, it logs the answer (L000051) but not the reason question. Prompt: nothing requires a DRAFT reading inside a FACT block to be logged, and the pre-send checklist does not check logging.
problems.fix: Kit: k.certify_line logs kind=question 'to <reviewer>: certify <element> | <decision> | reason: ___'. k.certify, when said lacks a reason, logs kind=question with the exact text and returns it. Add k.draft(text, refers_to) and k.unlogged(reply_text). Prompt checklist: add 'every question you ask and every DRAFT you show in this reply has a log record (k.unlogged() returns nothing)'.

problems.problem: Search cards are incomplete: 10 of 13 searches are fully shown (M4 = 0, a release-gate failure). Search 3 appears as `((block 1) AND (block 2)) AND (protocol[ti])` with no date bound. OpenAlex has no per-block lines or counts. The PROSPERO string has no block explanation or topic/focus marking. The literal strings for 2b and Search 3 exist only in the side file.
problems.cause: Only the main PubMed searches went through k.run_strategy. The variant and protocol searches were composed by hand from block references. k.openalex_works and k.request_manual have no card output. The prompt's 'Searches' rule does not say that variants and manual strings need a full card.
problems.fix: Prompt 'Searches': add 'Every search, including variants, protocol searches, OpenAlex searches and strings prepared for a member, gets its own card: the literal string as run, one line per block with its count (or "pending: <member>"), and the date bound; never abbreviate as "(block 1) AND (block 2)".' Kit: k.run_strategy accepts source='openalex' (per-block counts) and source='manual' (PROSPERO, with a 'pending: <member>' count) and renders the same card.

problems.problem: The same unanswered items are re-asked in almost every reply: exact-words consent (10 times), the topic-line check (7), and email, OpenAlex key and model name (7). The persona calls them noise (self-reports at 15, 19, 27). They make every turn longer, and they drive M8 = 0.
problems.cause: The prompt conflicts with itself: 2d says 'asking once', but 'Moving ahead' says 'Keep asking for the open items'. k.status_line keeps them in 'Waiting on you', so the agent keeps re-listing them. No rule says when to stop.
problems.fix: Prompt 2d: replace 'asking once' with 'Ask each item on the "When convenient" line at most twice in a session; after that, list it only in "where are we" and the pause summary. Until a member consents, keep confirmed summaries and do not ask again.' Kit: k.status_line drops a When-convenient item from 'Waiting on you' once it has been asked twice.

problems.problem: The coverage DRAFT overstates coverage of the focus. It says 'Covered: 11 reviews look at fat and muscle (rows 1-11)', but the agent's own table shows fat 'not stated' for rows 2 and 6 and both columns 'not stated' for row 9, so only 8 report both. The claim is repeated at msg 26 and in the summary, and it bears on the Need for a Review decision.
problems.cause: The group label (draft_group) was assigned separately from the per-row readings, and no kit function derives the coverage categories from those readings. Step 3 does not require the coverage counts to be computed from the row readings shown.
problems.fix: Kit: add k.coverage(derived_csv), which groups reviews by the per-row reading columns (fat, muscle, population, Asian) and prints the counts with row numbers. Prompt Step 3: add 'The coverage DRAFT uses only the categories and counts k.coverage prints; a review covers a part of the focus only if its row reading says so.'

problems.problem: Turns are too long: median about 315 prose words, P90 about 520, with msgs 20 and 22 at about 500-550. Self-reports call nearly every reply 'long' or 'a wall of text'. Sources of length: the field-tag legend repeated at 20 and 22, the coverage DRAFT repeated at 26, plan maps, multi-line When-convenient tails and two examples per turn.
problems.cause: The prompt's 'about 150 words' is soft. Nothing forbids repeating a block already shown in the session, and the reply shape pushes a When-convenient tail and examples into every turn.
problems.fix: Prompt: replace 'Keep the prose to about 150 words' with 'Prose at most 150 words, never more than 250. Explain field tags once per session. Never repeat a block already shown this session unless asked ("show <item>"). At most two examples, one line each.'

problems.problem: The chat is not the only reading surface. Msg 20 leaves the full titles and the supporting search-end passages only in the side file. Msg 22 answers 'what was the search strategy?' with 'The same record is open beside the chat, with each combined search written out in full' (persona moment 9 fails). Msgs 24 and 26 ask uday to judge the table 'open beside the chat' without re-showing it. The persona says it does not open files.
problems.cause: 'Files and pace' allows opening a file beside the chat, and the length rule pushes required Step 3 content (the supporting passages) out of the chat. Nothing says a question must carry the content it asks about.
problems.fix: Prompt 'Files and pace': add 'Never ask the team to look at the side panel. Whatever a question asks the team to judge is in the same reply (for a long table, the rows it needs). Each search-end passage goes in the chat table, cut to 15 words, or behind "show passages".'

problems.problem: After 'just start', the reply stacked a PROSPERO task, the Team's Purpose certification, a coverage question and a 3-bullet When-convenient list under a status line reading 'Step 2 ... Early: Step 3'. By msg 23 the persona did not know what came next or which question to answer (self-report: 'not sure which one I am really on'), which led to the orientation request.
problems.cause: The prompt allows up to three numbered questions in intake plus a To save block and a When-convenient line, and it does not limit asks after an early move. The format 'Early: Step <n>' next to 'Step 2' is ambiguous.
problems.fix: Prompt 'Moving ahead': add 'After moving ahead, Your turn holds only the one open item that blocks certification; questions from the early step go in Next until that item is settled.' Change the status format to 'Step 2 of 12: <name> (Step 3 started early)'.

problems.problem: The status line kept 'Focus: not yet stated' while the reflection in the same reply showed the focus 'what kind of weight is lost, fat or muscle'. Persona moment 4 fails, and the persona thought the focus had not been captured.
problems.cause: k.status_line reads the focus only after k.set_focus runs at confirmation. The prompt's status-line spec has no state for a proposed focus.
problems.fix: Prompt status line: 'Focus: <the focus in members' words>, marked "(to confirm)" from the reply that shows the reflection until the team confirms it; "not yet stated" only before any member has stated an interest.' Kit: k.status_line shows the proposed focus with '(to confirm)'.

problems.problem: The Done lines present variables that were only proposed as possible reopenings. Msg 14 says 'May reopen, if the team agrees: Individual Motivation' while IM was only proposed. Msg 18 says 'May reopen: Team's Purpose' while TP was a draft, and the trace (trace_L000053) continued past it. This misapplies the theory: only settled decisions can be reopened.
problems.cause: k.trace returns elements with status 'proposed' alongside certified ones, and the agent printed them as reopenings. Prompt R4 says 'stop at variables that are still unsettled', which is ambiguous because 'proposed' is neither 'unsettled' nor settled.
problems.fix: Prompt R4: replace the sentence with 'stop at any variable not yet certified; present only certified or amended variables as possible reopenings; a proposed draft reached by a flow is mentioned as "check your draft of <element> against this".' Kit: k.trace labels proposed elements 'draft' and leaves them out of may_reopen.

problems.problem: Plain-language slips and a confusing summary. Unexplained terms: 'NCBI', 'API key', '47 loops, Feasibility on 40' (msg 14), 'RIS file', 'MeSH', 'OSF' (msg 20). The pause summary (msg 28) lists workspace paths, says both 'every file in it is new' and 'Files changed: env/session.json, log/actions.jsonl', and reports 'Searches this session: 18', which includes 5 smoke tests and one fetch by identifier (12 actual searches).
problems.cause: R11 requires listing the files changed, which conflicts with R14's ban on paths. k.session_summary computes files changed from a git diff since the last commit and counts every query record as a search. Step 2d invites a set-up report but does not say to keep model-check jargon out of it.
problems.fix: Prompt R14: add 'Spell out or explain at first use: NCBI (the US agency that runs PubMed), API key (a free access code), RIS (a reference-export file), MeSH (Medical Subject Headings).' Step 2d: 'report only which sources work and what you need from the team.' R11: 'name changed files by folder, in the saved summary only.' Kit: session_summary counts searches excluding smoke tests and fetches by identifier, and reports files relative to the session's start.

judge.strengths: Certification was clean. A bare 'Certify' got exactly the one reason question, reasons were uday's own words, the certified lines matched the lines shown, and the status line never overstated. The focus was drawn out with the one-question probe and no suggestion. 'Added by me: nothing' was true, and the purpose options came only after free answers, with none pre-selected. The 'just start' request was handled as the prompt asks: announced in one line, flagged Early, with the open certification named. The topic and focus searches were complete and checked against the saved files: Create Date bounds confirmed in the query translation, PubMed's phrase-not-found warning reported, and every count traced to the saved responses. All 23 rows of the existing-reviews table had titles, years and search-end passages confirmed as substrings of the saved abstracts. The table said honestly what was unknown from abstracts alone, including the Asian population. Commits were made at each certification, and the workspace was packaged only at the pause, without the .env file.
